title: Chapter 225: Tape Recorder
html:
“Boss, you still want us to find him?” Xiao Du grumbled. Han Qiuming’s sharp tongue had left the young man with a poor impression of him.

“If we don’t find him, something might really happen.” Guo Miao’s expression was grave. “Something may have happened already. No—we can’t leave him behind. We’re going back now!”

“I agree, Boss.” To everyone’s surprise, Song An set aside his grudge and offered to help. “Splitting up inside a Haunted House is a mistake. We should stay together.”

Xiao Du nodded after a long pause. “Okay, I’ll follow you.”

Su Luoluo was the most bewildered of them all. Knowing none of the background, she had no idea what the Tian Teng Medical School employees were discussing. She simply followed as they ran back and forth.

“We need to search more carefully. Check every room.”

With Guo Miao in the lead, the group headed back through the Third Sick Hall.

…

Han Qiuming and Ye Xiaoxin entered the director’s office. A partition divided it into two smaller rooms, both furnished with simple desks and chairs.

“The drawers are empty, and the shelves hold no books. We can’t infer the director’s personality from his reading habits, but that saves us time. Many Haunted Houses hide passwords or clues inside books.” Han Qiuming directed his explanation at Ye Xiaoxin, though he might as well have been talking to himself. She moved away from him and ventured deeper into the office, where a large wardrobe caught her attention.

“Let me handle it. This wardrobe was obviously custom-made. There’s a ninety-percent chance a worker or trap is hidden inside.” Han Qiuming stepped forward and pulled open the door. The wardrobe was empty. He laughed awkwardly. “Looks like we found the other ten percent. The worker probably hasn’t returned from frightening Old Guo.”

Completely uninterested in him, Ye Xiaoxin tapped lightly on the wardrobe’s walls. “There must be a reason they placed a custom wardrobe inside a special room.”

When she knocked on the rear panel, the sound changed. The space behind it was clearly hollow. Working together, they removed the panel and exposed a hidden passage.

“The worker’s passageway?”

“I don’t think so.”

The passage was unlit, so Ye Xiaoxin switched on her phone’s flashlight. Once she and Han Qiuming had entered, an unseen force pushed the wardrobe panel slowly shut behind them. The passage was so cramped they could barely turn around, but fortunately, it was only a few meters long.

A steel door waited at the end of the oppressive tunnel. Ye Xiaoxin opened it and found a wooden panel beyond. She shoved the panel aside and emerged into an unfamiliar sickroom.

“The director’s office connects to a sickroom? Why would they design it that way?” Ye Xiaoxin had become completely engrossed in the Third Sick Hall’s authentic reconstruction.

“Perhaps the director kept a patient confined nearby for his private use,” Han Qiuming suggested. “I’ve heard that sort of thing was common when private hospitals were less strictly regulated.”

“Possibly.” They entered and began their inspection. The corners of the sickbed, tables, and chairs had all been rounded off. Otherwise, the sparse room seemed unremarkable.

“Let’s see what’s outside.” Han Qiuming opened the door, and a peculiar stench filled his nostrils—a blend of medicine and blood. He stumbled back a step before craning his neck to peer down the corridor.

The walls were cracked, and what looked like blood vessels pulsed behind them. The effect was deeply unnerving, as though the building were alive and the walls concealed its veins.

“I don’t think we’ve been in this corridor.” The set looked almost identical, yet its atmosphere was entirely different. The Third Sick Hall exploited its looping design to the fullest. Visitors could not see what lay at the end, nor could they know how many more corridors awaited them.

Worn mattresses covered the floor, with dolls poking their pillow-shaped heads from between them. Strange expressions had been drawn on their faces, and their eyes seemed to follow the pair. Han Qiuming wanted to retreat. They had entered through a secret passage, so they did not know how far they were from the others—or how many horrors this corridor concealed.

He aimed his phone’s light down the corridor. At the far end of the darkness was not an exit, but another corner.

“Don’t block the way.” Ye Xiaoxin stepped out of the sickroom, and a chill seemed to brush her legs. This corridor was clearly different from the previous ones.

“Let’s search. The tape recorder should be in one of these rooms.” Ye Xiaoxin entered the neighboring sickroom, but Han Qiuming remained where he was. Sweat slicked the hand gripping the doorframe as he looked back at the door they had just left.

Its upper half looked ordinary, bearing the number ‘3,’ but the lower half was disturbing. Bright, sticky red paint covered it completely. The color seemed alive, as though it were spreading across the door. “Room 3? Why are the room numbers in this corridor different from the others?”

Han Qiuming and Ye Xiaoxin searched the first three sickrooms. At the end of the corridor, they found a door with neither a number nor a sign. “Let’s see what’s inside.”

The room beyond was small and completely enclosed. Soundproofing covered the walls, a bed fitted with restraints stood in the center, and broken equipment lay beside it.

“This looks like an electroshock treatment room. I’ve seen similar ones in other mental hospitals and in movies.” Han Qiuming searched around the bed, then examined the pile of damaged equipment. A chuckle escaped him. “Found it!”

Han Qiuming moved the equipment aside to retrieve a tape recorder that was hidden among it.

“And here I thought this Haunted House would be difficult.” He tried to act unimpressed, but the excitement on his face betrayed him.

Ye Xiaoxin was far calmer. She studied the recorder and frowned for the first time since entering the Haunted House. “Do you hear that?”

“Hear what?” Han Qiuming had no idea what she meant. “Forget it. We need to leave. This game has a time limit, and I’m going to achieve a perfect clear and shut that Chen fellow up.”

“You truly can’t hear it?” Ye Xiaoxin pointed at the tape recorder in his arms. “The cassette is turning, and the play button is lit. It’s been running this whole time.”
